title: Athabaskan languages - Wikipedia
text: Athabaskan, also known as Dene, is a large branch of the Na-Dene language family of North America, located in western North America in three areal language groups: Northern, Pacific Coast and Southern.

title: Hupa language - Wikipedia
text: Hupa is an Athabaskan language spoken along the lower course of the Trinity River in Northwestern California by the Hupa and, before European contact, by the Chilula and Whilkut peoples, to the west.

title: The Athabaskan Language Family - Native American Netroots
text: The Athabaskan (also spelled Athapaskan and Athabascan) language family is found in the western American Indian culture areas. Linguists feel that the Athabaskan language family is one branch of a larger genetic grouping called Athabaskan-Eyak.
